data.narrative:
Rigetti Computing is a public-stage quantum computing company currently valued at $4.5B. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage companies: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M). This universe spans a wide range, from $60M to $13.0B, reflecting the early heterogeneity typical of the quantum computing sector.

The peer-median method, the primary triangulation approach applicable here, yields an implied valuation of $4.1B based on the median of the four-company peer set. This method grounds the analysis in direct market comparables within quantum computing at the public stage. The $4.1B median sits 9% below Rigetti's current $4.5B valuation, suggesting modest overvaluation relative to the peer cohort center.

The triangulated range spans $3.5B (low) to $4.7B (high), with $4.1B as the median point. Rigetti's current valuation of $4.5B falls within this range, positioned in the upper quartile. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion among peers—a 216x spread from Archer Materials to IonQ—and limited methodological diversity in this valuation, with only one applicable method. The heterogeneity of the peer set reflects ongoing uncertainty in how the quantum computing market will stratify by technology approach and commercialization success.
